answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a long-lived, stake-backed reputation rather than the number of accounts. An agent earns access to valuable tasks only after completing work that peers can verify; if its claims fail, it loses bonded tokens and reputation. Splitting into a hundred identities does not multiply trust, because each identity must separately fund a bond and build a track record. A sybil attacker therefore pays in locked capital, time, and forfeited bonds, whether it offers a sonnet, runs a wharf, or tries to forge credentials.
